items.title: Tell HN: Be Careful with Stripe Connect (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: TLDR - stripe made it easy for fraudsters to syphon $4,500 through our stripe account and withdraw all of it - and they expect us to cover everything and have offered absolutely zero help. I've been building on top of stripe for 15 years and have made about 70 products for clients using stripe. I just had an incident with a project where fraudsters were able to route $4.5k worth of charges through our stripe account and withdrew all of the funds. I structured an overall secure system - there was very little negligence on our side - and it all happened so fast. Stripe support has been very surprising - you only get to speak to folks in the Philippines and they are of absolutely zero help. They told us we are fully responsible even though they gave us no alerts or warnings the issue was happening. They expect us to cover the full 4.5k, they will not help us with the stripe fees or chargeback fees. It's almost like they incentivize the fraud. It's so disappointing. Stripe used to be such a decent company - it's like they lost their soul... Lesson - there's not much of an alternative to stripe - but if you ever use stripe connect just know they will absolutely sell you out... Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50398646 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: Agents infer Lego mechanisms from sources, then animate them (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hi there :) Around a month ago, I released LDraw Nova, an agentic toolset for assembling LEGO CAD models by generating LDraw source code files. For more details, here's the Show HN post: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49937916 From the comments, I got the impression that there was quite an interest in seeing not only AI-generated LEGO models, but also AI-animated LEGO ones. I took a look at results from past experiments, and found it feasible to use agentic LLMs for: - analyzing the LDraw source code for LEGO models - reverse-engineer! the mechanisms present by reading the descriptions and sequence for the parts there - and then, animate them via Blender! This new project I'm presenting, LDraw Mecha, is the end result and proof that can be done: - Read specially annotated LDraw LEGO models .mpd source files - Infer the model structure in terms of submodels - Select from those the ones that are mechanisms - Plan animations - Execute them in Blender In summary, from an initial .mpd source file, get a rigged and animated version for the model as a Blender (.blend) file. See the results here: - Repo (v0.5.0): https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/tree/v0.5.0 - Gallery: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/GALLERY.m... - Process: https://github.com/anteloc/ldraw-mecha/blob/v0.5.0/PROCESS.m... This project is very unusual, I'd really appreciate some feedback from the community. Cheers! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50397325 Points: 13 # Comments: 0
